subject: Request: brief retention carveout for volatile logs (Acme Health)
messages:
From: Laura Kim <laura@acmehealth.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com>
Cc: acme-security@acmehealth.com, Tom Bass <tbass@acmehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 01 Nov 2027 14:03:00 +0000
Subject: Short-term retention request — live triage for payment flow

Hi Aisha,

We're actively triaging a production failure in our payments flow that hit the EU region (eu-central-1). Our engineers need access to a set of ephemeral request/response logs and recent KV-cache snapshots that Redwood normally rotates and deletes within 24 hours.

Can Redwood hold the relevant tenant logs and kv-cache artifacts for an additional 72 hours while we investigate? We only need data tied to tenant_id=acme-prod-17 and the time window 2027-11-01 01:00–06:00 UTC.

Security team is copied — this is urgent for an incident post-mortem. Please let us know what info you need to approve a short-lived exception and any required paperwork.

Thanks,
Laura
Laura Kim
Director, Infrastructure — Acme Health

Attachment: support_request_4590.pdf (PDF, 48KB)
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com>
To: security@redwood.com, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Bass <tbass@acmehealth.com>, acme-security@acmehealth.com
Date: Mon, 01 Nov 2027 15:10:00 -05:00
Subject: Fwd: Short-term retention request — live triage for payment flow

Folks — forwarding Acme's request. They asked for a 72-hour extension to retain tenant logs/kv-cache for tenant_id=acme-prod-17 (EU). They flagged this as production triage; their security team is on the thread.

Quick Qs to unblock:
- Is a scoped, timeboxed retention carveout for 72 hours acceptable from our policy perspective?
- What controls must we apply (KMS key, access audit, read-only snapshot)?
- Who must sign off (security, privacy, legal)?

Connor — can you estimate operational steps (console API call vs. engineering runbook) and timing to enact the carveout? Monica — any privacy flags for EU data?

I attached their ticket. I attempted to pre-fill the authorization form they referenced (tenant_snapshot_authorization_form.pdf) — please review.

Thanks,
Aisha Rahn
Sr. Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com>, security@redwood.com
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Tom Bass <tbass@acmehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Nov 2027 08:24:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Short-term retention request — live triage for payment flow

Aisha / team —

Operationally we can implement a timeboxed carveout scoped to tenant_id=acme-prod-17 and the exact UTC window you specified. Implementation details:
- Create a retention override record in the Customer Ops console with TTL_override = 72h, scope=tenant, region=eu-central-1, reason=incident-triage-SUP-4590.
- Enforce read-only snapshot exports; block external exports while the override is active.
- Ensure the override is bound to a KMS key (customer or Redwood-managed) and log every read via our audit pipeline.
- Auto-expiry: the system will auto-reinstate default retention after 72h; no manual rollback needed.

Estimated lead time: ~45 minutes once security approves and we receive signed authorization from the ACME point of contact.

I'll prepare the console job and a short runbook snippet we can paste into the ticket.

—Connor
Director, Support Engineering
From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>, security@redwood.com
Cc: acme-security@acmehealth.com, Tom Bass <tbass@acmehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Nov 2027 09:02:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Short-term retention request — live triage for payment flow

Thanks Connor. Security/privacy notes:
- EU residency: since this data is in eu-central-1 and Acme has EU residency requirements, we must ensure no cross-region replication during the override.
- Data minimization: scope must be strictly tenant-only and the time window must be exact. No adhoc queries outside this window without a separate approval.
- Audit evidence: we will require a signed authorization from Acme's security lead and an internal approval record (I can attach the approval form once signed).
- Retention policy baseline: default ephemeral logs TTL is 24h for these artifacts; an exception to 72h is reasonable but should be the ceiling for production triage.

If Acme signs the form and confirms they understand the controls, I approve.

—Monica Patel
Privacy & Compliance Manager
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Cc: acme-security@acmehealth.com, Tom Bass <tbass@acmehealth.com>, Laura Kim <laura@acmehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 03 Nov 2027 15:41:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Fwd: Short-term retention request — live triage for payment flow

Approving a one-time, 72-hour, tenant-scoped retention override for tenant_id=acme-prod-17 in eu-central-1. Approval conditions:
- Acme must sign the attached tenant_snapshot_authorization_form.pdf and acknowledge the exact UTC window (2027-11-01 01:00–06:00 UTC).
- Override must use Redwood-managed KMS key with access restricted to Support Engineering and Security SREs; all reads trigger an immutable audit event.
- No external exports or backup snapshots allowed while the override is active.
- Connor: confirm when the override goes live and paste the console job id in the ticket.

Aisha — please relay approval to Acme and collect the signed form. I'll accept the confirmation email as the executive signoff once attachments are in the ticket.

Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Product & Operations — Redwood Inference

Attachment: approval_vivek_signed.eml (internal approval)
